title: Burst-threshold coordinator regression causing intermittent tenant underserve
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers using Dedicated reserved pools reported intermittent 503s and elevated tail latency during sustained multi-tenant bursts. Investigation shows the burst-threshold coordinator (component that enforces per-tenant burst caps and kickstarts burst replenishment) regressed after a scheduler refactor: lease renewals for short-lived burst tokens are sometimes delayed and the reclaim path aggressively marks tenant queues as 'saturated', which prevents downstream warmup and leads to under-allocation despite available headroom. Impact: affected tenants observed failed requests and silent throttling across several regions, primarily when many small tenants present frequent short bursts. Triggering conditions: high tenant-cardinality + many low-concurrency short requests with burst consumption near threshold. Repro steps: 1) Create 500 tenants with reserved pools and low steady traffic. 2) Send short 30–200 token bursts spaced at 200–500ms per tenant. 3) Observe allocator logs: repeated lease latency spikes and immediate saturation marks in coordinator. Root-cause hypothesis: a timing regression from the scheduler refactor introduced an ordering change between lease-renew and reclaim batching. Lease-renew RPCs can be delayed behind a periodic compaction job; reclaimed token accounting races with the burst-replenisher causing temporary negative effective credits. Temporary mitigation: 1) Enable coordinator debug sampling for affected regions (feature-flag: coord_debug_sample) to gather traces. 2) Roll out a protective heuristic to avoid flipping tenant state to 'saturated' unless two consecutive reclaim cycles indicate sustained deficit. 3) Short-term config change: increase burst-replenisher poll frequency from 500ms to 250ms for high-cardinality clusters. Long-term fix: revert ordering regression and add strong linearizability guarantees around lease-renew + reclaim (designing a small critical section), plus unit/integration tests that simulate high-cardinality short-burst workloads. Rollout plan: patch to runtime-1.24 branch -> canary in us-west-2 on a small reserved pool -> broader gradual rollout with feature flag gating. Customer comms: proactive notes to affected customers with temporary workaround and ETA for hotfix. Postmortem actions: add synthetic workload to CI, augment dashboards with per-tenant reclaim latency metric, and schedule a follow-up to review autoscaler invariants.
